# Stale Tests — freshness checking across KBs

-- note-stale.md --
---
type: note
title: Stale Note
updated: "2020-01-01"
confidence: high
---
This note is very stale.
-- note-stale.md --

-- note-fresh.md --
---
type: note
title: Fresh Note
updated: "2026-04-23"
confidence: high
---
This note is fresh.
-- note-fresh.md --

-- note-med.md --
---
type: note
title: Medium Note
updated: "2026-03-01"
confidence: medium
---
This note is somewhat stale.
-- note-med.md --

# Initialize first KB
exec akb init stale-kb-one
stdout 'Initialized KB .stale-kb-one. at .*'

# Initialize second KB
exec akb init stale-kb-two
stdout 'Initialized KB .stale-kb-two. at .*'

# Write stale page to first KB
cd stale-kb-one
exec akb write notes/stale.md <../../note-stale.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/stale.md'

# Write fresh page to first KB
exec akb write notes/fresh.md <../../note-fresh.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/fresh.md'

# Write medium page to second KB
cd ../stale-kb-two
exec akb write notes/medium.md <../../note-med.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/medium.md'

# Check stale across all KBs
cd ..
exec akb stale
stdout 'KB: stale-kb-one'
stdout 'STALE: notes/stale.md'
stdout 'KB: stale-kb-two'
stdout 'No stale pages'
stdout 'Total: 1 stale pages'
! stdout 'notes/fresh.md'

# Check --json output
exec akb stale --json
stdout '"kbs"'
stdout '"stale_pages"'
stdout '"total_stale": 1'
stdout '"name": "stale-kb-one"'

# Test exit codes - should exit 1 with stale pages
exec akb stale
! exit 0

# Add second stale page to make KB have no fresh pages
cd stale-kb-two
exec akb write notes/stale2.md <../../note-stale.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/stale2.md'

# Check stale again
cd ..
exec akb stale
stdout 'Total: 2 stale pages'

# Test empty registry warning
exec rm -rf stale-test-dir
exec mkdir -p stale-test-dir
exec HOME=$HOME:.test-home akb stale
stdout 'No KBs registered'
exit 0
